payload.headline: Netflix at 59.41 stays below fair value; add slowly, support near 56.31

summary.thesis: Netflix is a Grade B business priced at or below fair value on every method, but slowing sales and falling estimates argue for small, staggered buying.
summary.decision: Long-term add in small slices on dips; no swing trade while the downtrend holds.
summary.act_at: Add at 56.81 and 53.83; no buying above 64.9

payload.happening: Netflix closed at 59.41, up 0.92% on the day, but it is still in a downtrend below its falling 20-, 50- and 200-day averages (61.68, 66.24, 79.59). There is no new news since the last note. The next earnings report is on 2027-01-19, and analysts have cut this quarter's EPS estimate by 7.3% over 30 days.
payload.business: The core business is still strong. Over the last twelve months revenue was 49.7B, up from 43.4B. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) was 11.4B, up from 9.0B. Operating margin rose to 31.3% from 29.14%, and the share count fell 3.35% in a year. What is at risk is the pace. Quarterly sales growth slowed to 11.85% from 16.19% two quarters ago. The filings note that the 31% margin sits at the top of its 5-year range (17–31%), and peaks like that tend to fade. Debt of 12.7B is more than cash of 8.2B, so net cash is -4.4B. That is manageable against 11.4B of yearly free cash flow, but it is not a cushion. The small estimate cuts (next year EPS down 1.1% in 30 days) and the bearish options positioning (put/call open interest 2.47) mostly reflect sentiment. They do not change demand or margins today. No segment data is available, so this note cannot say which parts of the business are slowing.

worth.text: A discounted cash flow model (DCF: today's value of future cash) gives 38.59 in the bear case, 64.9 in the base case and 77.72 in the bull case, using a 9.9% discount rate. Valuing it on its own history of price-to-sales (price compared with yearly revenue) gives a range from 59.41 to 122.15, and today's price sits exactly at the low end. The price implies free cash flow starting to grow at 12.4% a year. That sits between the value at 10% starting growth (53.83) and at 20% (80.35). The gap between methods comes down to growth. The DCF bear case uses analysts' 5% EPS growth, while the history method assumes the stock gets back to its usual valuation. Margins are the other swing factor: if operating margin fell to 23% the value would be 60.0, and at 15% it would be 39.64. On multiples it trades at 16.9 times trailing earnings and 15.8 times next year's, with price-to-sales at 4.9 against a peer median of 6.8. My range is 53.83 to 80.35.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow starts growing at 10% to 20% a year, around the 12.4% the price implies, and operating margin does not fall much below 23%.

bull: Free cash flow grew to 11.4B from 9.0B, and the fcf margin is 22.87%.
Price-to-sales of 4.9 is below the peer median of 6.8 and at the 20th percentile of its own 5-year range.
Operating margin rose to 31.3% from 29.14%, while the share count fell 3.35% in a year.
bear: Quarterly sales growth slowed to 11.85% from 16.19% two quarters ago.
If operating margin falls to 15% from its 31.3% peak, the value drops to 39.64.
This quarter's EPS estimate was cut 7.3% in 30 days, and debt exceeds cash, with net cash at -4.4B.

levels.what: Top of the 56.31–56.81 support zone and the next small add. It is below the 60.0 value even if margins fade to 23%.
Value at 10% starting cash-flow growth and the low end of the fair-value range. This is the last planned add before the report.
DCF base value. Above it the margin of safety is gone, so no buying there.

longterm.why: At 59.41 the price is below the 64.9 DCF base and near the 60.0 value even with a margin fade to 23%. Estimates are still being trimmed and the trend is down, so adds stay small and staggered.

swing.why: The trend is down and the price is under every falling average. The first resistance at 61.14–61.64 is closer than support at 56.31–56.81, so there is little room above before sellers have shown up. No trade until a close above 65.08.

decision.timing: The 2027-01-19 report falls after the 2027-01-15 option expiry (which prices an 11.7% move) and before the 2027-02-19 expiry (17.1%), so adds stop at the 53.83 slice before the report, and further buying waits for a report that keeps operating margin near 31.3%.

change_mind: The next report shows operating margin falling toward 23% from 31.3%. That would pull value to about 60.0 and remove the discount.
The price closes below the 56.31 support while estimates keep falling (this quarter's is already down 7.3%). That would pause adds until the price reaches 53.83.
The price closes above the 65.08 resistance. That would break the downtrend and open a swing entry, with the 64.9 DCF base as the line where long-term buying ends.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still add, because the price at 59.41 remains below the 64.9 DCF base with no new news to alter the business picture.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
